q: Transition elements are the metals that exist in the block between Groups II and III, meaning they are in Groups _____ of the Periodic Table.
e: Transition elements are the metals that exist in the block between Groups II and III, meaning they are in Groups 3 to 12 of the Periodic Table. 1 to 2: groups 1 and 2 are s-block. Groups 13 to 18 are p-block.

q: Cupronickel alloy is an alloy of copper and nickel which is used in _____.
e: Cupronickel alloy is an alloy of copper and nickel which is used in shipbuilding. Jewellery is not the use named for this alloy here. Spacecraft is not the use named for this alloy here.

q: Transition elements are defined as elements that have partially filled d subshells or which can give rise to cations with _____ d subshells.
e: Transition elements are defined as elements that have partially filled d subshells or which can give rise to cations with incomplete d subshells. Empty is not the d-subshell requirement in the transition-metal definition. A completely filled d subshell is not the transition-metal definition.

q: The f-block lanthanide and actinide series are called the _____ transition elements.
e: The f-block lanthanide and actinide series are called the inner transition elements. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The first series 3d transition elements run from scandium through _____.
e: The first series 3d transition elements run from scandium through zinc. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The second series 4d transition elements run from yttrium through _____.
e: The second series 4d transition elements run from yttrium through cadmium. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The third series 5d transition elements run from lanthanum through mercury except 14 elements of the _____ series.
e: The third series 5d transition elements run from lanthanum through mercury except 14 elements of the lanthanide series. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The transition elements Zn, Cd, and Hg do not have the characteristic electronic configuration defined by the IUPAC because they have _____ d orbitals.
e: The transition elements Zn, Cd, and Hg do not have the characteristic electronic configuration defined by the IUPAC because they have completely filled d orbitals. An incomplete d subshell is the transition-metal signature.

q: The transition elements are also called the d-block elements because the _____ orbitals are filled in these elements.
e: The transition elements are also called the d-block elements because the d orbitals are filled in these elements. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The first row of the transition elements is in the _____ row (Period 4) of the Periodic Table.
e: The first row of the transition elements is in the fourth row (Period 4) of the Periodic Table. Fourth: transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: In the 3d series, there are _____ transition elements.
e: In the 3d series, there are 10 transition elements. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: All the transition elements in this series have quite similar radii, which accounts for their ability to blend together to form _____.
e: All the transition elements in this series have quite similar radii, which accounts for their ability to blend together to form alloys. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The decrease in atomic radii of 3d series occurs because the attraction force between the nucleus and electrons is _____ than the electron-electron repulsion force.
e: The decrease in atomic radii of 3d series occurs because the attraction force between the nucleus and electrons is equal than the electron-electron repulsion force. The because-clause is the chemical reason that makes the statement hold.

q: Compared to s- and p-block elements, the decrease in atomic radii across the 3d series is _____.
e: Compared to s- and p-block elements, the decrease in atomic radii across the 3d series is identical. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The first ionisation energies (IE) of scandium to copper increase only slightly as the positive charge on the _____ increases.
e: The first ionisation energies (IE) of scandium to copper increase only slightly as the positive charge on the atomic radius increases. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Towards the end of the 3d series, zinc has the larger atomic size and ionisation energy due to the increasing _____ as the occupancy of the d orbitals is completed.
e: Towards the end of the 3d series, zinc has the larger atomic size and ionisation energy due to the increasing nuclear charge as the occupancy of the d orbitals is completed. Ionisation energy is the energy you must put in to pull an electron off a gaseous atom.

q: In atoms of the transition elements, the _____ orbital is normally filled first and the rest of the electrons occupy the 3d orbitals.
e: In atoms of the transition elements, the 4s orbital is normally filled first and the rest of the electrons occupy the 3d orbitals. When these metals form ions, electrons come out of 4s first, then 3d.

q: The filling of the 3d orbitals generally obeys _____ rule, with one electron added to each of the five d orbitals before a second electron is added.
e: The filling of the 3d orbitals generally obeys Aufbau rule, with one electron added to each of the five d orbitals before a second electron is added. Hund's rule spreads electrons through a subshell before pairing. Pauli's: pauli limits one orbital to two opposite-spin electrons.
